title: On the sand
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies (the trilogy ran in print in three papers)
logline: Wednesday. The beach at the bottom. The dog on the sand, happy, which the strip draws exactly: the ears, the one bark at a wave. Then lying down. The way back up is not in this strip.

panels.composition: The beach. BARNABY walking the tideline, slow, ears up. WOOD sitting on the drift log.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, an old dog walking slowly along a tideline with its ears up while a man sits on a bleached drift log, muted wash, no words

panels.composition: The dog and a wave. One bark. Drawn as a small jagged shape.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, close-up of an old dog giving one small bark at an incoming wave, no words

panels.composition: The dog lying down on the wet sand. Not from tiredness, the strip insists — from choice. The way he did at four.

panels.composition: Wood on the log. The dog on the sand. The sea. The path behind them, up, not drawn.
